Bridge Retrofit Engineer said about it: Clamped preloaded High-Strength Friction-Grip, defined as High-Strength Friction-Grip (HSFG), bolts are used because the Load‐deformation behavior of injection bolts for maintenance of steel structures under dynamic loads (E24) regulates fatigue of preloaded bolts by detail category in EN 1993-1-9 and the Loss of preload in pretensioned bolts - TU Delft - [PDF Document] (E25) shows bolt relaxation can reduce fatigue life through loss of clamp load, so friction clamp without welds is the buildable load path.
Manager said about it: Structural Dynamicist is answered by carrying tune versus stroke and effective damping about 6.20 percent from the free-decay simulation (E17) into selection, Bridge Retrofit Engineer is answered by carrying stiffening need 46.5 percent from the stiffness-increase calculation (E27) and clamp-without-weld evidence in the injection-bolt behaviour source (E24) into bracket proof, Pedestrian Comfort and Safety Assessor is answered by holding Medium comfort as working target pending my Maximum versus Medium choice with Below Bridge Access Vehicle, defined as Below Bridge Access Vehicle (BBAV), access from the inspection-access rule (E49), Retrofit Integration and Construction Lead is answered by carrying twin 400 kg units from the per-unit split (E52) weighing 3.92 kN each from the per-unit weight calculation (E53) and the under-deck layout sketch (E55) into selection.
Bridge Retrofit Engineer said about it: I take from the 1 Experiments on coldformed steel momentresisting connections with 2 bolting frictionslip mechanism (E57) that slip capacity is calculated per EN 1993-1-8 assuming friction coefficient 0.3, which gives 32.9 kN design slip resistance per bolt from the slip-resistance calculation (E64) against 13.1 kN demand from the combined-load calculation (E65), so four bolts give redundancy; I take from the (PDF) Loss of preload in pretensioned bolts (E58) that preload loss must be checked, which confirms the fatigue concern in the Load-deformation behavior of injection bolts for maintenance of steel structures under dynamic loads (E24); this maps directly onto the seismic pipe-clamp friction attachment because I take from the Seismic Pipe Hanger: Secure & Reliable Support (E61) that friction-holding devices enable weld-free attachment and non-welded connections cut installation time, and from the UL CE Certified U Shaped Pipe Clamp with Quick Lateral Bracing Universal Hanger System (E62) that double U-bolts with lock nuts make a rigid connection resisting impact loads.
Bridge Retrofit Engineer said about it: I take from the 1 Experiments on coldformed steel momentresisting connections with 2 bolting frictionslip mechanism (E57) that slip is per EN 1993-1-8 with friction 0.3, giving 32.9 kN per bolt from the slip-resistance calculation (E64) against 13.1 kN demand from the combined-load calculation (E65), about seventeen body weights, so four bolts give redundancy; I take from the (PDF) Loss of preload in pretensioned bolts (E58) that preload loss must be checked with the fatigue concern in the injection-bolt source (E24), which from my discipline means annual Below Bridge Access Vehicle, defined as Below Bridge Access Vehicle (BBAV), re-torque per the inspection-access rule (E49) put by Retrofit Integration and Construction Lead, confirmed as serviceable from below with no deck hatch.

statements.text: Clamped preloaded High-Strength Friction-Grip, defined as High-Strength Friction-Grip (HSFG), bolts are used because the Load‐deformation behavior of injection bolts for maintenance of steel structures under dynamic loads (E24) regulates fatigue of preloaded bolts by detail category in EN 1993-1-9 and the Loss of preload in pretensioned bolts - TU Delft - [PDF Document] (E25) shows bolt relaxation can reduce fatigue life through loss of clamp load, so friction clamp without welds is the buildable load path.

Structural Dynamicist is answered by carrying tune versus stroke and effective damping about 6.20 percent from the free-decay simulation (E17) into selection, Bridge Retrofit Engineer is answered by carrying stiffening need 46.5 percent from the stiffness-increase calculation (E27) and clamp-without-weld evidence in the injection-bolt behaviour source (E24) into bracket proof, Pedestrian Comfort and Safety Assessor is answered by holding Medium comfort as working target pending my Maximum versus Medium choice with Below Bridge Access Vehicle, defined as Below Bridge Access Vehicle (BBAV), access from the inspection-access rule (E49), Retrofit Integration and Construction Lead is answered by carrying twin 400 kg units from the per-unit split (E52) weighing 3.92 kN each from the per-unit weight calculation (E53) and the under-deck layout sketch (E55) into selection.

I take from the 1 Experiments on coldformed steel momentresisting connections with 2 bolting frictionslip mechanism (E57) that slip capacity is calculated per EN 1993-1-8 assuming friction coefficient 0.3, which gives 32.9 kN design slip resistance per bolt from the slip-resistance calculation (E64) against 13.1 kN demand from the combined-load calculation (E65), so four bolts give redundancy; I take from the (PDF) Loss of preload in pretensioned bolts (E58) that preload loss must be checked, which confirms the fatigue concern in the Load-deformation behavior of injection bolts for maintenance of steel structures under dynamic loads (E24); this maps directly onto the seismic pipe-clamp friction attachment because I take from the Seismic Pipe Hanger: Secure & Reliable Support (E61) that friction-holding devices enable weld-free attachment and non-welded connections cut installation time, and from the UL CE Certified U Shaped Pipe Clamp with Quick Lateral Bracing Universal Hanger System (E62) that double U-bolts with lock nuts make a rigid connection resisting impact loads.

I take from the 1 Experiments on coldformed steel momentresisting connections with 2 bolting frictionslip mechanism (E57) that slip is per EN 1993-1-8 with friction 0.3, giving 32.9 kN per bolt from the slip-resistance calculation (E64) against 13.1 kN demand from the combined-load calculation (E65), about seventeen body weights, so four bolts give redundancy; I take from the (PDF) Loss of preload in pretensioned bolts (E58) that preload loss must be checked with the fatigue concern in the injection-bolt source (E24), which from my discipline means annual Below Bridge Access Vehicle, defined as Below Bridge Access Vehicle (BBAV), re-torque per the inspection-access rule (E49) put by Retrofit Integration and Construction Lead, confirmed as serviceable from below with no deck hatch.
